candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record features extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy and peri/pararenal soft-tissue infiltration strongly suggesting an underlying neoplasm, making paraneoplastic encephalomyelitis the reference diagnosis. ADEM shares overlapping MRI features (multifocal T2/FLAIR lesions, diffusion restriction) and is a plausible differential, but it asserts a post-infectious/post-vaccination immune etiology rather than a paraneoplastic one, representing an incompatible etiological subtype rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: ADEM is an immune-mediated demyelinating disorder typically post-infectious or post-vaccination, not a paraneoplastic process; the reference requires a paraneoplastic etiology tied to the systemic lymphadenopathy and soft-tissue infiltration suggesting occult malignancy

case_quality_flags: Systemic lymphadenopathy and soft-tissue infiltration strongly implicate occult malignancy; paraneoplastic antibody panel and tissue biopsy results not reported, leaving definitive confirmation pending
Rapid overcorrection of severe hyponatremia (117.5 to 146 mEq/L over 8 days) raises osmotic demyelination as a contributing or confounding diagnosis
